page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc7.xlarge is a compute-focused instance from the High Clock Speed family, configured with a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It provides 4 virtual CPUs derived from 2 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor running at a base clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The instance includes 8.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU), an L3 cache of 33 MB, and vector acceleration instructions including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support. No local storage is bundled, and it features a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight solid single-thread execution paired with moderate parallel capacity. In single-core tests, such as stress-ng (1578.29) and Geekbench (1336.0), the instance posts average results for its generation, supported by single-threaded compression throughput of 26.95 GB/s in gzip and 10.39 GB/s in bzip3. However, with only 2 physical cores and 4 vCPUs, aggregate multi-threaded metrics remain modest, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 2947.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 5062.05. Memory bandwidth reaches 30.99 GB/s for uncached read operations and 25.51 GB/s for write operations.

Without integrated local NVMe disks or high memory density, this instance balances lower operating footprint with high processor frequency. The ecs.hfc7.xlarge is suited for compute-bound microservices, lightweight web servers, compilation tasks, and front-end application routing where per-thread responsiveness takes precedence over parallel core scale or in-memory capacity.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc7.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance from the High Clock Speed family, designed for workloads prioritizing per-core clock frequency. Built on the x86_64 architecture using Intel Xeon 8369HB processors at 3.3 GHz, it features 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 8.0 GB of system memory, and a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not bundle local storage, relying on external block storage. Benchmark assessments show competitive single-core processing capabilities, including an average Geekbench single-core score of 1336.0 and steady single-threaded gzip compression at 26.95 GB/s. However, multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth are limited by the compact physical core count. The ecs.hfc7.xlarge delivers cost-efficient compute density for workloads such as application middleware, modest CI/CD build agents, and latency-sensitive web serving.
